the dose-saturation effect and the threshold-like response of tumor incidence in mouse skin are caused by tissue injury and its misrepair, respectively.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of the threshold-like dose-response of radiation-induced tumors in mouse skin.

the dose response of tumor development in mouse skin is not linear and is not proportional to the dose, and that the response is threshold-like.

radiation carcinogenesis in mouse epidermis is a complex and multifactorial phenomenon, and the dose-response curve of tumor development induced in this tissue by local irradiation is not linear, but is threshold-like.
the threshold-like response of tumor development is due to the tissue-mis-repair effect and is not due to the threshold effect of the cell killing.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the dose-saturation effect and the threshold-like effect are two sides of the same coin.
the tissue-misrepaired state is a necessary condition for tumor development and the threshold-like response is a manifestation of the tissue-mistreated state.
the threshold dose is not a physical quantity, but a biological quantity.
